title: An Efficient Polynomial Multiplication Derived Implementation of Convolution in Neural Networks
problem: Convolution is the most time-consuming kernel in CNNs and GNNs; existing libraries use either im2col+MM (introducing data redundancy) or FFT (requiring multiple passes), so no single implementation achieves optimal performance across all parameter configurations.
motivation: Achieving maximum convolution performance across diverse CNN/GNN architectures and parameter spaces requires novel approaches that avoid data redundancy penalties and multiple-pass overhead simultaneously.
method: The method expresses the convolution problem as polynomial multiplication: the filter and input patches are represented as polynomial coefficients, and multiplying those polynomials yields the convolution outputs as the result's coefficients. Using fast polynomial multiplication algorithms computes this in a single pass without duplicating data—avoiding both the data redundancy of im2col and the multi-pass overhead of traditional FFT convolution.
key_novelty: The key insight is expressing convolution as polynomial multiplication, which achieves efficiency gains unavailable through either standard im2col or FFT approaches alone.
contributions: A novel polynomial multiplication-based convolution formulation avoiding im2col redundancy and FFT multi-pass overhead
Implementation for multiple NVIDIA GPUs (3090Ti, V100, A10G) with PyTorch integration
Speedups up to 43.1% on V100, 34.6% on 3090Ti, 33.6% on A10G compared to cuDNN across broad parameter ranges
limitations: Scalability to very large convolutions, memory bandwidth utilization, and applicability to depthwise/grouped convolutions not discussed.
primary_theme: Polynomial multiplication formulation for efficient convolution
